diagnostic_evidence.quote: with the core tensor $\boldsymbol{\beta}^0$ and  the orthogonal Tucker factor matrices $V^{(\ell)} G^{(\ell)} \in \R^{n_\ell \times r_\ell^0}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed identity is false: $V^{(\ell)}G^{(\ell)}[G^{(\ell)}]^T[V^{(\ell)}]^T$ is an $n_\ell\times n_\ell$ matrix of rank at most $r_\ell^0<n_\ell$, so it cannot equal $I_{n_\ell}$. Column-orthonormality of $V^{(\ell)}$ and $G^{(\ell)}$ gives $[V^{(\ell)}]^TV^{(\ell)}=I_{r_\ell}$ and $[G^{(\ell)}]^TG^{(\ell)}=I_{r_\ell^0}$, and the correct identity establishing the proposition is $[G^{(\ell)}]^T[V^{(\ell)}]^T V^{(\ell)}G^{(\ell)}=I_{r_\ell^0}$. The proof's only step is therefore a false equation as written.

failure_location.quote: proves the orthogonality  $V^{(\ell)} G^{(\ell)} [G^{(\ell)}]^T [V^{(\ell)}]^T =I_{n_\ell}$, which completes the proof.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the displayed identity by $[G^{(\ell)}]^T[V^{(\ell)}]^TV^{(\ell)}G^{(\ell)}=I_{r_\ell^0}$, which follows from the assumed column orthonormality of $V^{(\ell)}$ and $G^{(\ell)}$.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Proposition prop:hybrid2Tuck contains a false displayed identity; the proposition's statement (existence of the rank-${\bf r}^0$ orthogonal Tucker representation) remains true.
issues.title: False orthogonality identity in the proof of Proposition prop:hybrid2Tuck
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction of the misordered product and identity dimension restores the proof; the statement and all downstream uses are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which forms a sequence of orthogonal polynomials on $[-1,1]$ with respect to the weight $w(x) = 1/\sqrt{1-x^2}$
The orthogonality property is based on the argument analogues to the  algebraic case but reformulated for polynomial arrays and note that the inner product should be properly weighted.

issues.failure_explanation: With the Chebyshev weight, $\int T_0^2 w\,dx=\pi$ but $\int T_k^2 w\,dx=\pi/2$ for $k\ge 1$, so for a Euclidean-orthonormal $V^{(\ell)}$ the Gram matrix of $v_j=\sum_i V^{(\ell)}_{i,j}T_{i-1}$ is $[V^{(\ell)}]^T\mathrm{diag}(\pi,\pi/2,\dots)V^{(\ell)}$, which need not be diagonal. Concrete counterexample: $m_\ell=2$, $V^{(\ell)}=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\big(\begin{smallmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{smallmatrix}\big)$ gives $v_1=(T_0+T_1)/\sqrt2$, $v_2=(T_0-T_1)/\sqrt2$ and $\int_{-1}^1 v_1 v_2 w\,dx=\pi/4\neq 0$. The proof's appeal to a 'properly weighted' inner product does not repair this, so the orthogonality assertion is false as stated.

failure_location.quote: If \cref{eqn:beta-Tucker} present the orthogonal Tucker tensor, then $\{T_{0:m_\ell-1}(x_\ell)V^{(\ell)}\}$ appear to be the set of $r_\ell^0$ orthogonal polynomials.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either restate the ChebTuck format in the $w$-orthonormalized Chebyshev basis ($T_0/\sqrt\pi$, $\sqrt{2/\pi}\,T_k$) with the coefficient tensor rescaled accordingly, in which case column orthonormality of $V^{(\ell)}$ does yield orthonormal factor polynomials, or delete the orthogonality assertion.
issues.overall_effect: The orthogonality claim in Proposition prop:funcTuck is false; the advertised 'orthogonal' two-level property of the ChebTuck format (echoed in the abstract's 'low-rank two-level orthogonal algebraic Tucker tensor') is unsupported. The conversion identity eqn:cheb_func_tuck itself is unaffected.
issues.title: ChebTuck factor polynomials are not orthogonal as claimed in Proposition prop:funcTuck
issues.why_classification: The claim sits in the statement of a proposition and its justification is invalid; repairing it requires a contained but real construction change (basis normalization propagating through the format definition and DCT scaling) or withdrawal of a stated structural property. No new global proof architecture is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We use the classical Tucker-ALS algorithm in our theoretical analysis and numerical experiments
where we also used the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and the relative truncation error $\varepsilon$ of the Tucker approximation in the last line.

issues.failure_explanation: Tucker-ALS is an alternating least-squares iteration that is only known to converge (at best) to a stationary point/local minimizer; no theorem establishes, and none is cited, that for every prescribed $\varepsilon$ it attains relative error $\varepsilon$ with quasi-optimal ranks. As a statement about the named algorithm it is false/unsupported, and it is what legitimizes the $\varepsilon$-relative-error hypothesis used in Proposition prop:cheb_tuck_error; in reality that hypothesis is a heuristic assumption on the achieved truncation, not a guaranteed output of Tucker-ALS.

failure_location.quote: It enjoys strong theoretical guarantees such that for any given $\varepsilon > 0$, it can approximate the original tensor in the sense of relative error $\|{\bf C} - \hat{\bf C}\|_{\mathrm{F}} \leq \varepsilon\|{\bf C}\|_{\mathrm{F}}$ with almost optimal rank parameters

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword the remark to state that quasi-optimal $\varepsilon$-rank approximations exist and are typically well approximated by Tucker-ALS in practice (or attribute any $\varepsilon$-accuracy guarantee to best-approximation/HOSVD-thresholding arguments rather than to ALS).
issues.overall_effect: The narrative that the proposed method comes with a guaranteed $\varepsilon$-accurate, near-optimal-rank Tucker decomposition is unsupported; the formal error bounds are conditional on the achieved truncation error and survive.
issues.title: Overstated theoretical accuracy/rank guarantees attributed to Tucker-ALS
issues.why_classification: A local rewording of the remark restores correctness; the formal results, which are conditional on the achieved relative error, and the numerical observations remain intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $\| \boldsymbol{\xi} \|_1 = \sum_{k=1}^{R} |\xi_k|$ is the $\ell_1$ norm of the normalization constants.

issues.failure_explanation: The triangle inequality applied to $\left|\sum_k \xi_k(\cdot)\right|$ yields $\sum_k |\xi_k|\,|(\cdot)|$, but the statement and the intermediate steps carry bare $\xi_k$. Since the weights are arbitrary reals (signed particle charges in the applications), the stated first bound can be smaller than, or even negative relative to, the nonnegative left side: e.g. $R=1$, $\xi_1=-1$, $\delta=0.1$, $d=3$ gives right side $-((1.1)^3-1)<0$. The first inequality of the lemma is therefore false as written for signed weights.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $\xi_k$ by $|\xi_k|$ in the first inequality of the lemma and in the corresponding steps of its proof.
issues.overall_effect: The first inequality of Lemma lem:ftilde-F is false for signed $\xi_k$; the final $\|\boldsymbol{\xi}\|_1$ bound, Corollary cor:added-1 and Theorem thm:added-1 use $\|\boldsymbol{\xi}\|_1$ and remain correct once the absolute values are inserted in the derivation.
issues.title: Missing absolute values on the signed CP weights in Lemma lem:ftilde-F
issues.why_classification: The forced insertion of absolute values is local and preserves every downstream statement; the main bound used in Theorem thm:added-1 is unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Similarly, the cost of trivariate cubic spline interpolation which is required in \cref{alg:cheb_tuck_alg} is $\mathcal{O}(m^3(m+n))$.
Construct the multivariate cubic spline interpolation $Q(x_1,x_2,x_3)$ of the data ${\bf F}$ on the uniform grid by, e.g., \texttt{interpn} in MATLAB.

issues.failure_explanation: Constructing the tensor-product cubic spline from the $n^3$ input values of ${\bf F}$ requires solving $O(n^2)$ tridiagonal systems of size $n$ (one per grid line per mode), i.e. $O(n^3)$ work — even reading the input costs $n^3$ — plus $O(m^3)$ for evaluation at the $m^3$ Chebyshev nodes. The stated estimate contains no $n^3$ term, and in the paper's regime $m\ll n$ it undercuts the true cost: for the paper's own parameters $n=2048$, $m=129$ the claimed $\approx 4.7\times10^9$ operations is less than $n^3\approx 8.6\times10^9$.

failure_location.quote: \cref{alg:cheb_tuck_alg}: $C_4 m^3(m+n) + C_5 m^3 + C_1 m^3 \log m + C_2 m^4 + C_3 m^4 |\log \varepsilon|$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the term $C_4 m^3(m+n)$ by $O(n^3+m^3)$ for the spline construction and evaluation.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised complexity guarantee for the full-tensor algebraic case (Algorithm alg:cheb_tuck_alg) is false (too small) precisely in the regime of interest; the estimates for Algorithms alg:cheb_tuck_func, alg:cheb_tuck_alg_cp and alg:cheb_tuck_alg_cp_2 are unaffected.
issues.title: Complexity bound for Algorithm alg:cheb_tuck_alg omits the O(n^3) spline construction cost
issues.why_classification: The repair changes a stated complexity guarantee by adding a dominant term in the relevant regime, so the advertised bound does not survive; but the correction is contained to one line of one proposition with no dependent formal results and no new proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: i.e., ${\bf p}_1, \cdots, {\bf p}_{15}$ can be well approximated by low-degree Chebyshev interpolants (left), while for short-range canonical vectors, the convergence is much slower (middle).
if we separate the long-range part of the potential by taking out the last $22$ canonical vectors, the error is reduced to the magnitude $10^{-6}$

issues.failure_explanation: The paper's own experiments identify the initial segment ${\bf p}_1,\dots,{\bf p}_{15}$ as the long-range vectors (well approximated by Chebyshev interpolants) and the later vectors $k=16,\dots,39$ as the short-range ones, and the lattice example obtains the long-range part by removing the last 22 of 50 vectors. Equation eqn:Split_Tens, however, defines the short-range part ${\bf P}_{R_s}$ as the sum over the initial segment $k=1,\dots,R_s$ and the long-range part ${\bf P}_{R_l}$ as the terminal segment $k=R_s+1,\dots,R$ — the opposite assignment. Taken literally, the ChebTuck approximation would be applied to the short-range component, which Table tab:single_newton_error shows cannot be approximated.

failure_location.quote: {\bf P}_{R_s} = \sum_{k=1}^{R_s} {\bf p}_k \otimes {\bf p}_k \otimes {\bf p}_k, \quad {\bf P}_{R_l} = \sum_{k=R_s+1}^{R} {\bf p}_k \otimes {\bf p}_k \otimes {\bf p}_k.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Swap the index sets in eqn:Split_Tens (equivalently, renumber the canonical vectors) so that ${\bf P}_{R_l}$ collects the smooth initial vectors and ${\bf P}_{R_s}$ the localized terminal ones.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed range-separation construction contradicts the rest of the paper; a reader implementing it literally applies the method to the wrong (short-range) tensor component, for which the advertised accuracy fails.
issues.title: Range-separation splitting assigns the long/short-range index sets opposite to the paper's own analysis
issues.why_classification: The correction is a swap of two index ranges; the numerical experiments already use the intended split and no labelled formal result depends on the formula.
